transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today? I'm here to help, so feel free to share whatever's been on your mind.

Um… thank you, doctor. I suppose it might sound a bit silly, but I’ve been having trouble with spiders. Not just disliking them, really—more that I’ve started arranging things at home so I don’t have to go where I might see one.

I put off doing laundry because the machine’s in the basement, and I avoid the garden shed if I can. Sometimes I even pay someone to do small jobs that I know I’m perfectly capable of doing myself, just because I can’t make myself go into those spaces. I know that probably sounds over the top… but it’s been getting in the way, and I thought I should finally ask for help.

When you avoid places like the basement or the garden shed, is it mainly because you’re worried about running into a spider, or is it more about feeling trapped or needing to perform certain routines to feel safe?

It’s mainly the spider part, I think. Not so much feeling trapped or needing to do a routine… I just sort of arrange things so I don’t have to risk seeing one.

I know it probably sounds a bit excessive, but yes, the basement laundry, the garden shed—those are the kinds of places I’ll avoid. And sometimes I’ve even paid someone to handle little jobs I should be able to do myself, just because I can’t quite make myself go in there.
